subject: Country-binding & failback: follow-up + clarifications from today's discovery
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Price <olivia.price@healthstack.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-18T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Country-binding & failback: follow-up + clarifications from today's discovery

Hi Olivia — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can map the right plan for HealthStack.

Call highlights (what I captured):
- Primary requirement: customer data used in inference must be bound to the United States (no persistent copies outside US regions).
- Cross-region failover is permitted for short-lived outages but only within US regions (e.g., us-east -> us-west).
- Backups: HealthStack asked about nightly backups, RPO target ~1h, RTO less than 4h; backups should be encrypted and, ideally, stored in US-only buckets.
- Logging: audit logs must show request/response metadata but PII must be redact-able; HealthStack will need at least 90 days of log retention with export capability for audits.

Questions for you so we don't miss anything:
1) By "bound to the US" — is the requirement that no data (including backups, cache/KV snapshots, or logs) may be stored outside US, or is cross-region ephemeral caching acceptable if it never persists beyond the request?
2) For failover: are you OK with automatic failover within the US regions, or do you prefer manual failover with an ops approval step?
3) Any specific KMS/HSM provider requirements (e.g., AWS KMS, customer-managed key) or key residency constraints?

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach a short SOC2 summary and a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that highlights the configuration options (strict country-binding vs. warm-standby in a secondary US region).
- If this looks good, let's book a 30-min follow-up with your security engineering team to nail the backup and logging controls. Suggested times: Wed/Thu next week.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary), HS-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP)

From: Olivia Price <olivia.price@healthstack.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: security@healthstack.com
Date: 2026-09-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Country-binding & failback: follow-up + clarifications from today's discovery

Thanks, Tessa — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- "Bound to the US": we cannot have any persistent customer data (including backups or archival snapshots) stored outside the US. Ephemeral in-memory caching is acceptable if you can guarantee it never gets written to disk or replicated to non-US regions.
- Failover: prefer automatic within-US failover for availability, but we need a configurable policy. For DR drills we will want a manual approval option.
- KMS: customer-managed keys are preferred; we use AWS KMS today. Can Redwood support CMK integration?
- PII & logs: request/response bodies may include PII. We need the ability to stop logging full request/response bodies for specified routes and to apply on-the-fly masking/redaction (e.g., replace SSNs/emails) before logs are written.

Also, one more ask — in case of a regional outage, what does your backup restore flow look like? Are there any cases where a backup copy could be restored into a non-US region?

I'll loop in our security lead on the follow-up call; can you share the MAP and SOC2 summary you mentioned?

Best,
Olivia
Director, Cloud Ops — HealthStack

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Price <olivia.price@healthstack.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-18T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Country-binding & failback: follow-up + clarifications from today's discovery

Olivia — quick technical notes to address the restore/failover questions (tl;dr: we can meet the US-only persistence constraint with configuration controls).

1) Ephemeral caching vs persistence:
- Redwood runtime uses an in-memory KV cache by default. That cache is not persisted to disk unless you enable snapshotting. We can guarantee in-memory-only behavior for specific routes so nothing is written to disk or replicated.

2) Backups & restores:
- Backups are configurable per-customer. Default backup targets are US buckets. There is no automatic cross-region restore into a non-US region unless a customer enables it. For HealthStack we will:
  - Configure backups to write only to US S3 buckets (customer or Redwood-managed)
  - Encrypt backups using customer-managed key (we support AWS KMS CMK integration)
  - Provide a documented restore playbook — restores into a secondary US region are allowed; restoring into non-US regions is blocked by policy and automation unless explicitly authorized and logged.

3) Failover model:
- We support two modes: automatic within-region-group (recommended) and manual-with-approval. Both modes preserve the storage binding constraints because we only failover within the list of allowed regions (you can supply that list).

4) Logging & PII controls:
- Flexible logging hooks: you can set per-route logging policies (full body, metadata-only, masked). Masking can be applied as a streaming transform so logs never contain raw PII.
- Logs can be routed to a US-only logging sink (CloudWatch/Sumo/ELK) and retained the 90 days you requested. Exports for audits are supported (CSV/JSON extracts).

If helpful, I can sketch a sample config block for the MAP that shows these toggles.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tessa
